newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CYPRUS, June 3 - Limassol - vessels due on 4/6 - 2 containers, 5 passenger. No delays expected. 5 container vessels discharging/loading at berth. 2 conventional vessels discharging. 1 vessel waiting at anchorage to discharge/load. Larnaca - vessels due on 4/6 1 container, 1 conventional. No delays expected. 1 container vessel discharging/loading at berth. 1 conventional vessel discharging at berth.

ISRAEL, June 3 - Haifa - Two vessels due. No delays expected, 2 general cargo, 2 bulk discharging at berth, 4 containers loading/discharging at berth, 1 tanker waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 1 under repairs/drydock, 1 awaiting orders. Ashdod - two to three days delay expected, 5 general cargo discharging at berth, 1 bulk loading at berth, 1 discharging at berth, 1 passenger vessel loading/discharging, 2 bulk vessels waiting at anchorage to discharge, 4 containers waiting at anchorage to load/discharge. Eilat - one general cargo loading at berth, 1 bulk loading/discharging at berth, 1 passenger vessel loading/discharging at berth.
JORDAN, May 31 - Ababa - One vessel loading at berth, 7 discharging at berth, 1 waiting at anchorage to load, 2 waiting at anchorage to discharge, 1 awaiting orders.

MOZAMBIQUE, June 2 - Nacala - port working normally (first come, first served basis). No restriction on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restriction of 9.5 at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tugboat available. Beira - general cargo berths working normally. 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres LOA. Some restriction for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with Port Captain. Max. draft for 24 hour navigation 7.5 metres. 2 tugs available. General access channel 2 waverider buoys have been deployed in the approach channel. Maputo - berthing/sailing of 24 hours for vessels up to 120 metres LOA. Some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with Port Captain. All berths fluid. Draft restriction in the channel is 9 metres less 0.5 metres plus rise of tide of the day. Max. draft for 24 hour navigation is 9 metres.
NAMIBIA, Walvis Bay - June 2 - working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, June 2 - Richard's Bay - General cargo berths fully committed next week. Bulk import berths berth 701 open until 4/6, then fully committed. Berth 702 fully committed. Bulk export Berths (minerals etc.) Fully committed from mid-week. Bulk coal Berths 4 vessels alongside. 10 anchored. 13 due by 9/6. Delays of approx. 3 days being experienced.

Durban - container terminal delays of up to 4 days can be expected whilst 2 new cranes are being positioned at the container terminal. Point/New Pier/Maydon wharf berths working normally for general cargo vessels.

Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) 3 vessels due in June. Bunker supplies fluid. This Could change daily due to bunching of vessels. East London - General/combi terminal/tanker berth extremely busy, but no delays expected. Dry-dock open for bookings. Two tankers due weekly.

Port Elizabeth - working normally. 7 vessels in port. 1 fruit vessel anchored awaiting orders. No delays at general, fruit or tanker Berths. Ore berths, 1 ore vessel berthed. 48 hours delay. 2 vessels Due by 8/6 with berthing delays of between 36 and 48 hours expected. Container berth, 9 vessels due by 7/6. Barge with gantry crane due 4/6. Therefore only one berth available with 2 cranes. Berthing delays of between 12 and 24 hours due to strike, with only 5 gangs working on fruit vessel and log loader. Both gantries in operation.

Cape Town - breakbulk berths (general cargo) no delays expected. Fruit berths fully occupied. Container terminal working normally with vessels berthing and working on arrival. Bunker berths vessels berthing and bunkering on arrival. Drydock and repair quay fully occupied and booking essential. Saldanha bay - working normally.

TUNISIA, May 31 - Gabes - two vessels loading at berth (bulk fertiliser, bulk phosphate). 2 vessels discharging at berth (bulk Barley, bulk sulphur). 1 bulk sulphur waiting at anchorage to discharge. Tunis - three general cargo vessels in port. 3 awaiting instructions. Rades - two ro/ro vessels in port. Goulette - North side, 1 passenger vessel, 1 cereal vessel. South side, 1 vessel Discharging grain, 1 loading clinker. 2 vessels in roads (cereal). Sousse - four vessels in port of which 1 discharging grain, 1 discharging PVC, 1 loading, 1 bulk cargo, 1 other vessel. No waiting Time. No vessels awaiting orders. Sfax - five vessels operating of which 3 loading fish, 1 discharging sulphur, 1 discharging bulk Wheat.

TURKEY, June 3 - Mersin - Eleven vessels awaiting orders. 12 Vessels operating of which loading 1 pumice stone, 1 container vessel, 2 cement, 1 livestock. Discharging, 1 sugar, 1 other cargo. Loading/discharging 1 vehicle, 3 container vessels, 1 vehicle/containers/other cargo. Free zone piers - 1 vessel discharging sugar, 1 loading cotton, 1 loading rice. Seka - one vessel discharging fertiliser. Istanbul - Haydarpasa 6 vessels operating of which 3 containers, 1 dry cargo, 2 ro/ro. No berthing delays. Galata - 9 cargo/passenger vessels operating. Port congested. Ambarli - 15 Vessels operating. No berthing delays.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, Dubai, May 31 - 31 vessels due. No delays expected. 3 containers loading at berth. 1 under repairs/laid up. General cargo 7 vessels due. No delays expected. 5 vessels discharging at berth. 3 under repairs/laid up). Tankers, 6 tankers due. No delays expected. 8 tankers under repairs/laid up).
